title: podman pull to include architecture variants for all platforms by default
body:
### Feature request description

The OCI image spec[1] now includes platform variants for non-aarch64 platforms.

To support this fully, `podman pull`, should include the variant for all platforms per the specification.

As distros start to have a default minimum microarchitecture, like RHEL10 with x86_64 being v3+, helping users avoid downtime by being explicit of the microarchitecture at retrieval time would be useful.

Thankfully can be explicitly done. Being more explicit removes the burden of a user diagnosing a SIGILL/SEGV when an unsupported image is retrieved.
```
$ podman   pull --variant v3  registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi
Trying to pull registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi:latest...
Getting image source signatures
Checking if image destination supports signatures
Copying blob 1f0d847c2422 skipped: already exists  
Copying config 76819081c1 done   | 
Writing manifest to image destination
Storing signatures
WARNING: image platform (linux/amd64) does not match the expected platform (linux/amd64/v3)
```

Obviously registries will need to start being more explicit too.

its was pointed out that containerd/ https://github.com/containerd/platforms and other parts may been to be updated first.

In the meantime the fallback, (client or registry?) seems to work ok with warning.

[1] https://specs.opencontainers.org/image-spec/image-index/#platform-variants

### Suggest potential solution

A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.

comments.body:
Its unclear what exactly you are expecting us to do here. Just that if there is more than one x86_64 image in the manifest with different variants we pick the best one according to what the current system supports?
I think there was some conversation happing around that somewhere already but I do not think that ever took off.

Just as basic counter example images are commonly pulled, locally build and then pushed again and pulled somewhere else. If the builder is newer than the final consumer you will break them. Same for things where people pull + save the image and then load it elsewhere.

I am sure the problem space is something that can and likely should be improved but I am not sure we could alter the default behavior without breaking a bunch of people.

Also there is a larger long standing issue around multi arch support that our store can represent each name just once, pulling a different arch or variant would untag the the other local image for the newly pulled one, so later runs likely pick up the wrong thing.
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26621

>  Just that if there is more than one x86_64 image in the manifest with different variants we pick the best one according to what the current system supports?

That's basicity it, extends to other platforms too of course. With obviously the same problems mentioned.

> Just as basic counter example images

yes. This is generally true of the platform even without a variant that its assuming the target is the same platform. But sure, its a change in behaviour for those that don't expect it.

Maybe as a non-default option `--variant-match` to keep current behaviour the same. A "later variant %s available, if for local host use" info message maybe.

The long standing issue around multi-arch storage (that I do hit on a not infrequent basis), isn't actually made significantly worse by the functionality as any solution would already be considering platform and variant.
